T: He wrote to her every day for a year.
D: A mill worker and a rich girl fall for each other one South Carolina summer, and the story of it is read to an old woman in a nursing home.
P: Serve the cobbler when Allie remembers it is their story.
S: Spiced boiled peanuts. Off the Ferris wheel.

Rinse the peanuts and put them in a big pot with 3 litres of water, the salt, Old Bay and bay leaves. Weigh them down with a plate, bring to the boil and simmer until the shells are soft and the nuts are tender. Leave them in the brine for 10 minutes, then drain and serve warm with lemon.
Lowcountry crab cakes with remoulade. 365 letters.

Mix the crab, egg, 3 tbsp mayo, mustard, half the panko, spring onions and half the lemon juice, then shape into 8 small cakes. Press the cakes into the rest of the panko and chill for 10 minutes. Stir the 125g mayo with the capers, paprika and remaining lemon for the remoulade. Fry the cakes in the oil until golden on both sides and serve with the remoulade.
3 tbsp whole-egg mayonnaise, plus 125g for the remoulade@Pantry
M: Bird for bird buttermilk fried chicken
Buttermilk fried chicken. If you're a bird, I'm a bird.

Soak the chicken in the buttermilk with a big pinch of salt, at least 2 hours or overnight. Mix the flour, paprika, garlic powder and salt, and dredge the chicken until shaggy. Fry in oil at 170C, turning, until deep gold and cooked through. Warm the honey with the chilli flakes and toss the cabbage and carrot with the mayo and vinegar. Drizzle the chicken with hot honey and serve with the slaw.
8 chicken thighs, bone in, skin on@Meat
Prawns over creamy grits. The Windsor house, rebuilt.

Bring the milk and 500ml water to a simmer and whisk in the grits; cook, stirring, until thick and soft, then beat in half the butter and the cheddar. Fry the bacon until crisp, then add the garlic and the rest of the butter. Add the prawns and cayenne and cook just until pink, then squeeze over the lemon. Spoon the prawns over the grits and scatter with spring onion.
W: Peach cobbler with cream. Read aloud every day.

Toss the peaches with the brown sugar, cornflour and cinnamon and tip into a baking dish. Rub the butter into the flour and caster sugar, then stir in the buttermilk to a soft dough. Drop spoonfuls over the peaches and bake at 190C until golden and bubbling. Serve warm with cold cream.
6 ripe peaches, sliced (or 2 x 825g tins, drained)@Produce
K: Middle of the street bourbon sweet tea
Bourbon sweet tea over ice. Allie and Noah lie down in the middle of the street.
Steep the tea bags in 800ml just-boiled water, then stir in the sugar and cool. Fill 4 glasses with ice, peach and lemon. Pour in the bourbon and top with the sweet tea.
